value.body: A credit analyst studies the finances of borrowers, such as businesses or individuals, to judge whether a loan can be given and on what terms. Employers include banks, NBFCs, credit rating agencies and financial services firms. A typical day involves analysing financial statements, preparing credit notes, and following up on documents and risk flags.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com, BBA or MBA Finance; CA or CFA helps

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, financial statements, credit bureau reports

items.label: Key outputs
items.value: Credit appraisal notes and risk ratings

items.label: Credit rating agencies registered with SEBI
items.note: Three of them are listed companies

items.label: NBFC credit as a share of GDP
items.note: Up from 13.5% a year earlier; NBFCs employ many credit analysts alongside banks
items.source: RBI, Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024-25

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often enter as credit or risk trainees in banks and NBFCs, or as analysts at rating agencies, many through campus hiring. MBA graduates fill a large share of corporate credit roles.

value.title: At a glance
items: Retail credit roles tend to have more openings than corporate credit.
Next roles: senior credit analyst, credit manager, risk manager.
Professional qualifications (CA, CFA, FRM) help with corporate and rating roles.

competition.note: BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
